newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end mixed, BHEL jumps on results.
newsitem.headline: India shares end mixed, BHEL jumps on results.

text.p: ** (1245 GMT) - Indian stocks close mixed on late
profit-taking after prices rise for most of the day
** Bombay's top 30-share index up 0.60 pct at 3.559.65
** Lack of fresh political developments dulls trade
** State-run BHEL jumps seven percent after firm's net
** National exchange index up 0.71 pct at 1,009.30
** Delhi index drops 0.15 pct at 750.02, Calcutta 0.35
Indian stock markets showed small gains on Thursday during a lull in the country's five-day old political crisis with the government facing a confidence vote in parliament, dealers said.
"The markets are moving sideways," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James India Ltd. "There is not much downward pressure, but the market is stuck in a narrow band."
State-run BHEL -- among the country's top 25 firms -- said its net profit surged nearly 34 percent to 4.68 billion rupees ($130 million), from 3.5 billion rupees in 1995/96.
BHEL shares vaulted 21.75 rupees, or nearly seven percent, to 351.75 rupees after the firm announced its results.
"The stock rocketed after the announcement of results. Speculators were aggressive bidders," said a dealer at a local brokerage. By close, 813,800 shares were traded at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Amidst the lack of political developments, pressure mounted on the Congress to strike a bargain with the government.
Brokers said they were pinning hopes on the safe passage of the 1997/98 (April-March) pro-business budget despite a current political crisis.
